gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold chief complaint only documents diarrhea. Generated adds vomiting and explicitly ties the 3-day duration to chief complaint. Diarrhea and 3-day duration are supported (cc-001, hpi-001; hpi-008 supports vomiting but not as part of chief complaint). Inclusion of vomiting in the chief complaint is an addition, not clearly supported by the gold CC text.
Three-day history of diarrhea matches hpi-001. Description ‘initially watery’ matches watery stools (hpi-002); ‘now very loose’ is a mild elaboration but consistent.
Frequent BMs, at least four times today, aligns with ‘already 4x by midday’ (hpi-007). Slightly different phrasing but consistent.

Generated: ‘has a fever’ described as boiling but not measured. Gold: ‘feels hot but hasn’t checked temperature’ (hpi-017). Gold stops short of diagnosing fever; generated asserts fever as present, which overstates and conflicts with the documented uncertainty.

Frequent vomiting is supported by ‘Vomiting’ (hpi-008). ‘Unable to retain fluids or food’ is consistent with ‘doesn't feel like she is holding down fluid’ (hpi-009); inability to retain food is a plausible extension, so overall supported.

Timing of last vomiting episode (two hours ago after breakfast) is not present in gold facts. Gold only notes vomiting and difficulty keeping fluids down (hpi-008–009) without episode timing; thus this is new information.
Abdominal pain around the navel that comes and goes matches periumbilical cramps coming in waves (hpi-005).
Pain often accompanying an urge to defecate is consistent with pain worse when needs to open bowels (hpi-006).
No blood in stools is supported (hpi-004). However, gold does not mention urine blood at all, so ‘no blood in urine’ is an added, undocumented detail.
Generated PMH: menstrual cramps. Gold PMH: nil (pmh-001). This introduces a past condition that contradicts ‘no significant past medical history.’

Gold: ‘Vitamins’ (med-001) but no specification. Generated: ‘vitamin D daily’ with missing dose/route/frequency. The fact that she takes a vitamin is supported; specifying vitamin D and daily schedule are additions beyond gold.
Occasional ibuprofen for menstrual cramps is not mentioned anywhere in gold facts, so this is new medication history.
Gold mentions ORT regularly with difficulty keeping it down (hpi-015) but not ‘three times a day for past two days.’ The specific dosing schedule is new and therefore an addition.
Gold does not mention allergies. ‘None reported’ is extra information not derivable from gold data.
Brother has similar symptoms matches fh-001 and hpi-013.
Denies smoking matches ‘Non smoker’ (sh-002).
Occasional alcohol, ‘a pint from time to time,’ is consistent with drinks 1 pint a week (sh-003); phrasing is looser but not contradictory.
Works as graphics designer matches ‘graphic designer’ (sh-004).
Lives with her brother and mother matches sh-001.
Primary assessment acute gastroenteritis matches impression ‘Gastroenteritis’ (asm-001).

Gold asm-001: ?Viral/?food poisoning; fh-001/fh-002 show similar family symptoms suggesting infectious. Generated: likely viral gastroenteritis, possibly infectious given family member – the viral/infectious rationale is supported, but gold also posits food poisoning, which is not reflected. So this is partially aligned but omits the food‑related aspect and reframes the differential.

Gold explicitly documents diarrhea (hpi-001), vomiting (hpi-008), abdominal cramps (hpi-005), and feeling hot but not measured fever (hpi-017). Generated lists diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and abdominal pain as supporting symptoms. The inclusion of fever as an established symptom conflicts with the uncertain fever status, while the other symptoms are supported. Hence mixed: supported for diarrhea, vomiting, pain; contradictory for fever.

Risk of dehydration due to inability to retain fluids is consistent with ‘doesn't feel like she is holding down fluid’ and ongoing vomiting/diarrhea (hpi-001, hpi-008–009), so the assessment is a reasonable interpretation.

Gold asm-001: Gastroenteritis ?Viral/?food poisoning. Generated differential: viral vs bacterial gastroenteritis. Viral is supported; bacterial is not mentioned in gold and ‘food poisoning’ is omitted. So this is partially aligned (for viral) and additive (for bacterial) while missing the documented food poisoning possibility.
Advising to continue ORS/ORT in small sips to maintain hydration matches gold plan-002.
Simple diet with toast and biscuits is not in gold. Gold only mentions avoiding fruits/vegetables/milk (plan-003); bland diet recommendation is an added detail.
Avoid fruits, vegetables, and dairy matches ‘avoid fruits, vegetables, and milk’ (plan-003).

Instruction to monitor hydration status and report worsening symptoms is not explicitly stated in gold. Gold follow‑up (fu-002) instructs to contact clinic for worsening/abdo pain/unwellness, but specific ‘monitor hydration status’ self‑direction is new, so overall this is additional framing.

The actions and rationale match, but generated omits the condition ‘if fever persists’ and treats the plan as unconditional; therefore partially aligned with some added/assumed implementation detail.

Outpatient with urgent clinic follow‑up for further assessment aligns with gold fu-001 urgent appointment; disposition as outpatient is consistent with no admission mentioned in gold.
